fields.title: Cardiac ablation
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Cardiac arrhythmias are serious disturbances of the heart rhythm that can affect quality of life and even lead to severe complications such as stroke or heart failure. Over recent decades medicine has taken significant steps in developing innovative treatments for arrhythmia. One such turning point has been cardiac ablation, an innovative procedure that opens a new era in the treatment of heart rhythm disorders.

Methods of diagnosis

Accurate diagnosis is the foundation of successful treatment for cardiac arrhythmia. Modern diagnostic methods allow doctors to determine the type and mechanism of the arrhythmia precisely, which helps in choosing the best approach to treatment. The main methods of diagnosing arrhythmia include:

  • Electrocardiography (ECG): one of the most widely used methods, recording the electrical activity of the heart and revealing abnormalities in its work.
  • Holter monitoring: continuous ECG recording over a long period (usually 24 to 48 hours) to detect infrequent arrhythmias that an ordinary ECG may miss.
  • Echocardiography: an ultrasound method that allows the structure and function of the heart to be examined and possible anatomical causes of arrhythmia to be identified.

Methods of treatment

Traditional treatment for arrhythmia may involve drugs such as antiarrhythmic agents, or the use of an implantable cardioverter defibrillator for severe arrhythmias. In recent years, however, cardiac ablation has become the preferred treatment for many arrhythmias.

  • Drug treatment: in milder forms of arrhythmia the doctor may prescribe medicines such as antiarrhythmic agents, beta blockers or other drugs to stabilise the heart rhythm and prevent arrhythmia.
  • Implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD): a device used to detect and stop life-threatening arrhythmias. An ICD can automatically return the heart to a normal rhythm or perform cardioversion, in which a controlled electrical discharge resets the arrhythmia.
  • Continuous patient monitoring: for patients with infrequent or symptomatic arrhythmias the doctor may decide to fit a continuous monitor, which records the heart rhythm over a long period and allows arrhythmias to be detected and analysed.
  • Catheter ablation: a minimally invasive procedure carried out with catheters passed through the blood vessels into the heart. By applying controlled heat (radiofrequency ablation) or cold (cryoablation) to the abnormal areas of heart tissue, the specialist destroys the sources of the arrhythmia and restores a normal heart rhythm.
  • Surgical treatment: in some cases, particularly where the arrhythmia is linked to structural abnormalities of the heart, surgery may be needed, such as major surgical ablation or the implantation of marker electrodes.
  • Pacemaker implantation: a pacemaker may be fitted to maintain an optimal heart rhythm in patients with arrhythmia or bradycardia.
  • Implantation of a cardioverter defibrillator (ICD): in cases of serious arrhythmia or a risk of cardiac arrest, the doctor may recommend an ICD to detect and stop life-threatening arrhythmias automatically.
  • Cardiac surgery: in some complex arrhythmias, particularly alongside other heart disease, surgery may be needed to eliminate the sources of the arrhythmia and restore normal electrical activity of the heart.

Every treatment for arrhythmia is chosen individually, depending on the type of arrhythmia, its severity, the patient's general condition and other factors. A combination of methods may be used to achieve the best results in treating arrhythmia and preventing complications.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Israel is widely recognised as a medical centre of world class, and its cardiology departments are equipped with the latest technology. Treatment of arrhythmia, including cardiac ablation, in Israel has a number of advantages:
  • Highly qualified specialists: cardiologists and electrophysiologists at Israeli clinics have many years of experience and extensive training, which ensures that procedures are highly effective.
  • Use of advanced technology: medical institutions in Israel make active use of advanced technologies and treatment methods, which improves the results of cardiac ablation.
  • An integrated approach: Israeli clinics bring together various fields of medicine, which allows patients to receive comprehensive and individual care for arrhythmia.

Conclusion

Cardiac ablation is a revolutionary approach to treating heart rhythm disorders that can considerably improve patients' quality of life and reduce the risk of complications. Modern methods of diagnosis and treatment make the procedure safer and more effective. Israel is considered one of the leading countries in cardiology and cardiac ablation, which makes it an attractive place for the treatment of arrhythmia. If you have problems with your heart, do consult a cardiologist and ask about the possibility of ablation to restore a normal heart rhythm and improve your health.

fields.title: Pituitary adenoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Pituitary adenoma: advanced treatment in Israel

A pituitary adenoma is a benign tumour of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland that can affect the production of hormones regulating important functions of the body. In Israel patients receive a comprehensive and individual approach to the diagnosis and treatment of pituitary adenoma, including modern methods of investigation and therapy.

Diagnosis of pituitary adenoma:

  1. Hormone tests
    Measuring hormone levels in the blood to identify disturbances linked to the work of the pituitary gland.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    The main imaging method for studying the adenoma in detail and assessing its size and shape and its effect on the surrounding tissue.
  3. Ophthalmological examination
    Assessment of the visual fields and other eye functions to determine the effect of the adenoma on the optic nerve.
  4. Angiography
    Examination of the blood vessels of the brain, which may be carried out to rule out other vascular conditions or in preparation for surgery to remove the adenoma.

Methods of treating pituitary adenoma in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment
    The use of medicines to reduce the size of the tumour and correct the hormonal balance.
  2. Surgery
    Transsphenoidal adenomectomy — minimally invasive removal of the adenoma through the nasal sinuses. This method is used most often because of its effectiveness and safety.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Including the Gamma Knife and proton therapy, used where surgery is not possible or the adenoma has not been completely removed.
  4. Targeted and hormonal therapy
    For the treatment of certain types of adenoma that actively produce hormones.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach
    The treatment plan is drawn up taking account of every aspect of the patient's health, including the size and type of the adenoma, its hormonal activity and the patient's general condition.
  • A multidisciplinary team
    Endocrinologists, neurosurgeons, ophthalmologists and radiologists work closely together to ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Access to advanced technology
    The use of the most modern medical technologies and treatment methods, minimising risks and side effects.

Treatment of pituitary adenoma in Israel is aimed at removing the tumour or controlling its growth, restoring normal hormone levels and preserving the patient's quality of life.

fields.title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
fields.bodyHtml:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia: modern treatment in Israel

Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also known as an enlarged prostate, is a common condition among men over 50. Israel applies the latest advances in medicine to treat it effectively, improving patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of benign prostatic hyperplasia:

  1. Physical examination,
    including a rectal examination of the prostate.
  2. PSA blood test
    (prostate-specific antigen) to assess the risk of prostate cancer.
  3. Ultrasound examination
    (transrectal ultrasound) of the prostate through the rectum to determine the size of the gland.
  4. Uroflowmetry
    — measurement of the rate and volume of urine passed, to assess the degree of obstruction of the urinary tract.
  5. Questionnaires, such as the IPSS symptom index, to assess the severity of symptoms.

Methods of treating benign prostatic hyperplasia in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Alpha blockers to relax the muscles of the bladder neck and prostate.
    • 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors to reduce the size of the prostate and lower the PSA level.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Transurethral microwave thermotherapy (TUMT).
    • Transurethral needle ablation (TUNA).
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) — relief of obstruction of the urinary tract.
    • Laser enucleation of the prostate — a modern method with minimal blood loss and rapid recovery.
    • Adenomectomy (open prostatectomy) — used where the prostate is very large.
  4. New technologies:
    • Aquablation — the use of a high-pressure water jet to remove prostate tissue.
    • Prostatic urethral lift — a newer treatment aimed at reducing pressure within the prostate and improving urine flow.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified doctors: Israeli specialists have extensive experience and an international reputation in urology.
  • Innovative medical equipment: clinics are equipped with the latest technologies for diagnosing and treating BPH.
  • An individual approach: every patient is given a personal treatment plan that takes account of his circumstances and preferences.
  • Comfort and support: patients receive full support through diagnosis, treatment and recovery.

Treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia in Israel allows men to regain comfort in daily life, reducing symptoms and preventing the possible complications of this condition.

fields.title: Adenomyosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Adenomyosis: advanced treatment in Israel

Adenomyosis is a gynaecological condition in which tissue resembling the endometrium (the lining of the uterus) begins to grow within the muscular wall of the uterus. It can cause severe pain and heavy periods. Modern methods of diagnosing and treating adenomyosis are available in Israel, allowing women to restore their quality of life.

Diagnosis of adenomyosis:

  1. Ultrasound examination:
    Transvaginal ultrasound is the main method of diagnosing adenomyosis, allowing the structure of the uterus and any abnormal areas within the muscular wall to be seen.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used to obtain more detailed images of the uterus, particularly in complex or unclear cases.
  3. Laboratory tests:
    Although there is no specific test for adenomyosis, tests may be directed at assessing general health and identifying associated conditions.

Methods of treating adenomyosis:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Hormonal therapy: the use of oral contraceptives or hormonal intrauterine systems to reduce menstrual bleeding and ease pain.
    • Antigonadotropins: drugs that suppress ovarian function and reduce the growth of endometrial-like tissue.
  2. Surgical treatment:
    • Conservative excision: removal of areas of adenomyosis while preserving the uterus, used where a woman wishes to retain her fertility.
    • Hysterectomy: removal of the uterus may be recommended in severe cases or where other treatments have not worked.
  3. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Uterine artery embolisation: a procedure that blocks the blood supply to areas of adenomyosis, causing them to shrink.
  4. Physiotherapy and supportive treatment:
    • Programmes for managing pain and stress, physiotherapy exercises and relaxation techniques can help improve general health and reduce symptoms.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: every patient receives a personal treatment plan based on her particular clinical picture.
  • Use of the newest technologies: access to advanced medical innovations and treatment methods.
  • A multidisciplinary team: gynaecologists, fertility specialists, endocrinologists and others work together to ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment.

Treatment of adenomyosis in Israel is aimed at minimising symptoms, preserving reproductive health and improving the quality of life of women affected by the condition.
